name: Alligator Creek Falls
description:
21st September – Alligator Creek Falls
Walk Leader: Amanda Drilling
RSVP: Amanda at ajdrill@gmail.com
Walk Rating: Grade 3

Short Description: 
17 km return, approximately 5–6 hours including breaks. Out-and-back trail with multiple creek crossings and an optional swim at the falls.

Walk Description: 
This trail traverses through Bowling Green Bay National Park, following the Alligator Creek trail to the falls. The distance is 17 km return and should take around 6 hours including breaks. There will be multiple creek crossings (expect one to be waist deep), so shoes and clothes will get wet.

For those keen to brave the cold water, there will be an opportunity for a swim at the base of the falls.

name: Ladies' Track, Castle Hill, Townsville
description:
Friday After-Work Walk – The Ladies’ Track 🌿

Have you heard of or walked the Ladies’ Track? 

Join the Townsville Bushwalking Club on Friday evening for a short after-work adventure up one of Castle Hill’s most historic and newly restored trails.

📍 Meet: Cutheringa Trail Head car park, 5:00 pm sharp
📍 RSVP: You must RSVP with Luen luenwarneke@gmail.com
🚶‍♀️ Walk: The Ladies’ Track up Castle Hill (Grade 2)
⏱ Distance & time: ~2 km | ~30 min ascent
⬇️ Return: Walk down via the road ~30min
💵 Cost: Free for members | $5 non-members (insurance cover)

This well-established track features stone stairs, treated timber steps, and a flat contour path cut into the hillside, making for a relatively easy and scenic climb atop of the lower cliffs. The walk traces the historic route once used during WWII, when “female friends” would discreetly visit soldiers stationed at the Pillar Boxes atop Castle Hill.

Restored in 2025, the Ladies’ Track ascends from the western side near the water tank, winds around beneath the cliffs and Jenkinson’s Post Lookout, and connects into the Pill Box Walk. Along the way, you’ll spot sections of original stone steps and enjoy a unique perspective of Castle Hill.

✨ A great way to add variety to your Castle Hill walks, and perfect for a relaxed Friday evening leg-stretch before the weekend!

name: Hughenden Explore
description:
30th to 31st - Hughenden Explore

Join us for an unforgettable remote adventure out near Hughenden, where we’ll explore a spectacular and rarely visited locations. This trip will combine hiking, caving, and canyoning through a stunning but fragile landscape. Expect cool nights (possibly below 10°C) and warmish days (25°C+), rugged off-track terrain, and plenty of time immersed in nature. This is a remote, self-sufficient trip — you’ll need to bring all your own food, water, and camping gear, and be prepared for minimal facilities, no mobile reception, and an environment where safety, preparation, and Leave No Trace principles are essential.

It’s roughly a 5+ hour drive from Townsville to the trailhead, with the final stretch on dirt roads. A high-clearance 4WD is recommended but not essential. We’ll be tackling Naga, one of the more accessible places in the area, and camping in a beautiful remote setting. 

If you’re ready for a challenging, rewarding, and truly off-the-beaten-track experience, email me at luenwarneke@gmail.com to express your interest and get the full details.

name: August 24th: Many Peaks/Mount Marlow
description:
August 24th - Many peaks/Mount Marlow

Walk leader: Amanda Drilling

RSVP: ajdrill@gmail.com

Rated-  Level 2. You should have at least attempted Castle Hill. This is not for the absolute beginner, mainly due to the heat and time this walk will take. 

Duration:  Approximately 4 hours. 12km circuit.

What to expect: Moderate level of fitness required. Expect some steep, uneven and rocky sections. 

There are exposed sections, so expect it to be hot. Shaded areas often have a lot of very friendly mosquitos so bug deterrents are a must. The pace will be moderate and continuous, so we can cover the distance within the designated time-frame and enjoy our stops at the points of interest mentioned above.

TBWC Members: Free

Visitors: $5 (You can become a member after 3 club walks!)

name: Smell the flowers
description:
Morning bushwalking team!

We have an additional option on the 16th/17th August with a rough plan to head up to Hughenden to camp and do some exploring and short walks. It's flower time at the moment so it will be a spectacular sight!

The rough plan is to meet up at 10am Saturday the 16th. Then explore and do some short walks in the afternoon on Saturday and Sunday morning. Possible places to explore would be the normal gorge, Five Fingers, sunset view and possibly on sunday the sword gorge area. The short walks will be off track, scrubby, with some steep climbs in wonderful sandstone country.

If you're keen please email the club info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com 

You will need to arrange your own National Park campsite booking and travel to the site. Vehicles should be high clearance and don't be afraid of getting your car scratched (there is a bit of overhanging vegetation on the tracks). And bring some firewood!

name: August 16th-17th: Paradise beach overnight
description:
August 16th-17th

Paradise beach overnight

Walk leader: Brent Campbell

Grade: 5
RSVP: townsvillebushwalkingclub@gmail.com (Limit: 15 people)
🏕 QPWS camping permit required



Join us for an overnight adventure to Paradise Beach on Cape Cleveland’s remote western coastline. We’ll follow a flagged but faint bush track through semi-evergreen rainforest and coastal scrub, eventually arriving at the pristine sands of Paradise Beach. 

The journey involves rough terrain, off-track navigation, and minimal shade, making it a Grade 5 walk recommended for experienced hikers. An optional exploration of Castle Rock (weather and time permitting) is also a possibility for those keen.
Bring 6 L of water (minimum), all your overnight gear, food, and be fully self-sufficient. Note that there are no water sources or facilities.

TBWC Members: Free

Visitors: $5 (You can become a member after 3 club walks!)

name: Killymoon Creek
description:
Sunday, 3rd August
Killymoon Creek
Led by Molly Hoey

RSVP : molly.hoey1@gmail.com
Places Limited to 15


Level - Beginner friendly, off track, creek hopping

Where to Meet:
7 am - will advise via email to those that have RSVPd. 

Walk Description:

Killymoon Creek, in the dry season, is a fantastic spot for rock-hopping enthusiasts. This walk start on a fire trail on private property with a few good hills to get everyone warmed up. The creek bed starts as a series of small rocky gullies which soon open up into a spectacular gorge.

We will take lunch at the swimming hole, where the polar bears amongst us can have a dip before lunch. This will be our turn around point and we will descend back down the creek from here.

This adventure will see us tackling numerous kinds of climbing. You will need to have a suitable level of fitness and coordination.

How long:

Full day walk. Estimate back at the car park around 4 pm.

What to bring:

Advised equipment: Water (at least 4L as we cannot guarantee suitable water from the creek), Lunch (Snacks and electrolytes), Basic first aid, suitable sun safe clothing, sun screen, Mozzie spray and suitable shoes.

Speciality equipment: I strongly advise gloves as this walk requires a lots of hand work (but that’s just personal preference). You will need boots with plenty of tread for grip.


RSVP 

To RSVP, please get in touch with Molly Hoey - molly.hoey1@gmail.com. 

Non-members/Guests = $5 club fee to participate.
